override.reason: Automated design review is unavailable while being rewritten (per project policy). User (Subho) reviewed and approved this LLD revision in chat after I presented its summary, checklist results, and rationale.

summary.prose: This Story lets an operator pin a dedicated security-review model, independent of the core/mid/cheap tiers every other reasoning site uses, and have that pin checked for availability before a security review runs -- a malformed or unreachable pin is reported as a specific blocker, never silently replaced with a different model. This revision corrects the LLD's own contract text: the configuration field that carries the pin must be a required, always-present three-way result (nothing configured / a valid pin / a malformed pin), not the optional field originally sketched, because only the three-way shape lets the selection logic refuse a malformed pin instead of treating it the same as nothing configured.

hldContextSlice.frameworkSummary: The Epic adds a standalone orchestration module (outside src/workflow/review-round/) that owns model selection, dependency-advisory collection, code-assessment execution, and reporting, and supplies review-round's existing RoundDriverHooks.security hook as a thin adapter. review-round itself stays unchanged except for the one call site invoking that hook; the data shapes it already exports (SecurityFinding, SecurityLocator, EvidenceProvider, VerificationReceipt) are populated, never redefined.

ownedContracts.name: SecurityModelSelection
ownedContracts.purpose: Carries s1's resolved security-model identity (or its unavailability) across the boundary so s3 can dispatch the code-vulnerability pass through CliProvider.runReadOnlySession with that exact model, record the effective model in the report without re-resolving it, and refuse with the blocker reason rather than falling back silently.

boundary.internal: Model-tier resolution (extending src/config/role-taxonomy.ts with a security role), availability/credential checks, and the no-silent-fallback blocker-reporting logic stay private to s1; only the resolved SecurityModelSelection crosses its boundary. s1 must also specify the configuration contract for an INDEPENDENTLY selectable security-model binding (distinct from core/mid/cheap) and its interaction with coreFloor enforcement and unavailable-model handling; this is s1's central, still-open design question.

hldContextSlice.rolloutPhase: Phase A -- foundational contracts (model selection and dependency-advisory collection)

api.name: parseSecurityModelPin

parameters.name: models
parameters.purpose: The raw, already-parsed `models` object from config.json (or an equivalent in-memory config source) to read the `security` key from.

returns.meaning: A required, always-present tri-state: {kind:'absent'} when no models.security key is set, or it is set to the catalog's own '' runner+model unset sentinel; {kind:'valid', runner, model, effort?} when models.security validates to a listed CLI family + non-empty model; {kind:'malformed', detail} for anything else present (wrong shape entirely, or an incomplete/mistyped object).

preconditions: models is the raw models.* config object, not yet validated
postconditions: The result is one of exactly the three SecurityModelPinResult variants; never undefined.
An absent key and a malformed value are never conflated: only {kind:'absent'} falls through to the role's tier-default model downstream.

api.name: resolveSecurityModelCandidate
api.signature: function resolveSecurityModelCandidate(cfg: AnalyzeConfig, registry: ModelRegistry, repoPath?: string): SecurityModelCandidate

parameters.name: cfg
parameters.purpose: The loaded analyze config, carrying cfg.tiering.security (the SecurityModelPinResult) and cfg.tierResolutions.

parameters.name: registry
parameters.purpose: The model registry used to check a pin's listedness and capability floor.

parameters.name: repoPath
parameters.purpose: Optional repo path, so a repo's own models.byRepo[repoPath].tasks['security.review'] / coreFloor override is honored when computing the fallback floor tier for an absent pin.

returns.meaning: status:'candidate' with the selected (runner, model, effort?) when a listed, floor-eligible model was found (either the explicit pin, or -- only for a genuinely absent pin -- the 'security.review' role's own tier-default model, resolved via the same byRepo->global->role-default precedence + coreFloor clamp every other role uses); status:'unavailable' with blockerReason otherwise. Takes cfg.tiering.security's kind directly: 'malformed' always resolves to 'unavailable' immediately, never falling through to a tier-default model.

preconditions: cfg.tiering.security is the tri-state SecurityModelPinResult (never undefined).
postconditions: A malformed pin, or a pin/tier-default model that is unlisted, below-floor, or whose tier resolution itself carries a silent-substitution fallback, never resolves to 'candidate'.

interactionWithShared.howDetails: sc1 (SecurityModelSelection) is not produced by the functions this revision documents -- resolveSecurityModel (src/config/analyze.ts:505-546) produces it, by calling resolveSecurityModelCandidate first. This revision only corrects the internal AnalyzeTiering.security field the candidate resolution reads; sc1's own shape (owned by s1, consumed by s3) is unaffected and is not re-specified here.

errorCases.scenario: models.security.runner is set but models.security.model is missing or empty (a genuine config mistake)
errorCases.detection: parseSecurityModelPin checks runner and model independently; only both being absent or both being the catalog's '' unset sentinel reads as {kind:'absent'} -- one set without the other is {kind:'malformed'}.
errorCases.response: resolveSecurityModelCandidate returns status:'unavailable' with the parser's detail string as blockerReason immediately, never falling through to the role's tier-default model.
errorCases.userImpact: The security review reports the specific misconfiguration (e.g. 'models.security.model: expected a non-empty string') instead of silently reviewing with a different model.

errorCases.scenario: models.security is present but the wrong shape entirely (null, a string, an array, a number)
errorCases.detection: parseSecurityModelPin treats sec === undefined as the only absent case; any other non-object value is {kind:'malformed'}, distinct from a genuinely absent key.
errorCases.response: resolveSecurityModelCandidate refuses immediately with status:'unavailable', same as any other malformed pin.
errorCases.userImpact: A config author's typo (e.g. models.security: 'claude') is reported as a malformed configuration, not silently treated as unset.

errorCases.scenario: No pin is configured, and the role's own fallback-tier model was itself silently substituted (unlisted/rejected) by the registry
errorCases.detection: resolveSecurityModelCandidate checks cfg.tierResolutions[floorTier].fallback for the absent-pin fallthrough path.
errorCases.response: Refuses with status:'unavailable', naming the fallback.reason and fallback.requested, rather than silently using the registry's own substitute model.
errorCases.userImpact: The operator is told their configured tier model was rejected, instead of the security review silently running on an unrequested substitute.

errorCases.scenario: The caller's opts.signal is already aborted before resolveSecurityModel is called, or is aborted while the probe is outstanding
errorCases.detection: resolveSecurityModel checks opts.signal?.aborted at function entry before any dispatch; an abort while outstanding is caught by an 'abort' listener on the caller's signal.
errorCases.response: Resolves immediately (pre-aborted case) or as soon as the abort fires (in-flight case) with status:'unavailable' and a cancellation blockerReason; an internal AbortController is aborted in both cases and its signal is threaded into the underlying CliProvider.complete() call, which genuinely stops the CLI subprocess and bypasses its retry chain rather than leaving it running past the deadline.
errorCases.userImpact: A cancelled review stops promptly and does not leave a background CLI process retrying after the caller gave up.

edgeCases.input: models.security: {runner: '', model: ''} -- the catalog's own persisted 'unset' default, written by config reconciliation on every ordinary install
edgeCases.expected: Reads identically to no models.security key at all: {kind:'absent'}, falling through to the role's tier-default model.

edgeCases.input: A valid pin with effort: '' (the catalog's documented 'use the CLI's own default' value)
edgeCases.expected: The '' effort is stripped before the {kind:'valid'} result is returned; it is never forwarded as a literal --effort '' to the CLI.

alternativesConsidered.name: Required, always-present tri-state SecurityModelPinResult (as built)
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: AnalyzeTiering.security: SecurityModelPinResult, a discriminated union {kind:'absent'}|{kind:'valid',...SecurityModelPin}|{kind:'malformed',detail}, never undefined.
alternativesConsidered.approach: parseSecurityModelPin(models) always returns one of the three tagged variants; parseTiering wires it onto AnalyzeTiering.security unconditionally (never collapsed to undefined). resolveSecurityModelCandidate(cfg, registry, repoPath?) switches on cfg.tiering.security.kind: 'malformed' refuses immediately (status:'unavailable', never falls through to the role's tier-default model, satisfying ac1's 'reports the blocker without a silent fallback'); 'absent' falls through to the role's own tier-default model (resolved via the same byRepo->global->role-default precedence + coreFloor clamp every other role uses); 'valid' is checked against the listed-model + capability-floor requirements like any pin. This is the smallest shape that lets resolveSecurityModelCandidate's own fixed signature (cfg, registry) distinguish all three states without any raw models.* access.
pros: The only shape that lets a function receiving just (cfg, registry) distinguish absent from malformed -- the Story's own fail-closed requirement (ac1: 'reports the blocker without a silent fallback') depends on this.
Matches parseTieringOverride's own established pattern of a single parse function owning validation + fail-soft/fail-closed semantics for one config area.
Zero raw models.* access needed downstream; AnalyzeConfig stays the single source of truth for every reasoning site.
cons: Deviates from the originally-sketched optional SecurityModelPin|undefined field in this Story's own narrative -- requires this LLD revision to document, since the field is no longer optional.

alternativesConsidered.name: Optional SecurityModelPin | undefined (original sketch)
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: AnalyzeTiering.security?: {runner, model, effort?} | undefined -- absent and malformed both read as undefined.
alternativesConsidered.approach: parseSecurityModelPin returns a SecurityModelPin when models.security validates, or undefined otherwise (silently dropping a malformed entry, mirroring parseTieringOverride's existing tier-entry convention). resolveSecurityModelCandidate(cfg, registry) checks cfg.tiering.security !== undefined and falls through to the role's tier-default model whenever it is undefined.
pros: Smaller type surface; mirrors the pre-existing tiers.* parsing convention exactly, no new tri-state concept introduced.
Fewer lines of validation code in parseSecurityModelPin.
cons: Cannot satisfy ac1: a user who sets models.security.runner='cli-claude' but forgets model gets exactly the same undefined as a user who configures nothing -- the malformed pin silently falls through to the tier-default model instead of refusing, which is the silent-fallback this Story's own acceptance criterion forbids.

resolveSecurityModelCandidate(cfg, registry) has no other signal (no raw models.* access, per the LLD's own fixed signature) to recover the distinction -- the information is destroyed at parse time and cannot be reconstructed downstream.
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Violates ac1 and k2: a malformed pin collapses to the same undefined as an absent one, so resolveSecurityModelCandidate(cfg, registry) silently falls through to the tier-default model instead of refusing -- the silent fallback both constraints forbid.

alternativesConsidered.name: Two separate optional fields (presence + error)
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: AnalyzeTiering.securityPin?: SecurityModelPin | undefined plus AnalyzeTiering.securityPinError?: string | undefined, read together.
alternativesConsidered.approach: parseSecurityModelPin populates securityPin when valid, or securityPinError (a detail string) when malformed; both undefined means absent. resolveSecurityModelCandidate checks securityPinError first (refuse if set), then securityPin (use if set), else falls through.
pros: Avoids introducing a discriminated-union type; each field is a simple optional.
Achieves the same absent/valid/malformed distinction as a1 ac1 requires.
cons: Two fields that must always be read together and are mutually exclusive by convention only (nothing in the type system prevents both or neither being set, unlike a1's exhaustive discriminated union) -- a future caller could read securityPin without checking securityPinError and silently treat a malformed pin as absent.

Less idiomatic than a1 relative to this codebase's existing tagged-result conventions (e.g. TierResolution's own fallback field) and the AnalyzeTiering interface's own documentation comment, which already states the tri-state is 'always present'.
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Functionally satisfies the same constraints as a1 today but with a non-exhaustive two-field convention that can silently regress to a2's failure mode if a future caller reads securityPin without checking securityPinError.
